Because of its low melting point (327°C) and malleability, lead was
the foundational metal smelted in Anatolia long before Bronze or Iron,
anchoring humanity's continuous toxic exposure baseline.

g.text: COAL EMERGENCE: CHINA TO ROMAN BRITAIN

text.tspan: Used in China (4000–2000 BCE) and described in Theophrastus' On Stones
(c. 371 BC). By the end of the 2nd century AD, the Romans exploited coal
across all major coalfields in England and Wales for metallurgy.
Coal is a massive source of Pb and heavy toxins. Combined with metal
smelting and urban smoke inversions, British and German industrial
cities reached existential human perturbation thresholds by 1850.

g.text: Quantifying Environmental Perturbation on the Human Condition
BAILEY ET AL. (2018): WWI RECRUIT STUNTING

text.tspan: Linked 1901 British census to WWI enlistment records. Childhood coal
pollution caused a 0.56-inch (OLS) to ~1.0-inch (IV using 1851 coal
intensity) loss in final adult male height. Comparing to the total 2.75-inch
secular height gain from 1890s to 1970s, this is massive proof that
environmental perturbation stunted biology prior to WW1 and WW2.
Studied acute London smoke inversions: air pollution spikes triggered
immediate excess mortality. Proved lethal comorbidity synergy where the
presence of measles and tuberculosis dramatically multiplied the mortality
impact of coal air pollution across urban populations.

g.text: CLAY ET AL. (2018): 1918 INFLUENZA PANDEMIC MORTALITY

text.tspan: Leveraged 1915 data on coal-fired electricity plants. Proved coal air
pollution heightened susceptibility to viral pathogens and severely scaled
respiratory complications, driving catastrophic 1918 pandemic deaths.

g.text: Overcoming the Isolation Fallacy • Genome, Biome, Immunome

text.tspan: Science routinely fails by isolating single chemical insults. In biological
reality, insults have been continuous and compounding across evolution,
migration, UV, radon, and geology, now multiplied by the Anthropocene.

g.text: Ruhr Imperial Ambition & American Coal Expansion

text.tspan: German heavy coal and metallurgical dominance in the Ruhr Valley fed
the neurological and industrial engine for global conquest in WW1 & WW2.
In the US, coal-fired trains propelled industrial genocide across the West.

g.text: The Clean Air Act (1970) Proof vs Modern 1/3 Burden

text.tspan: When emissions fell after 1970, human health, cognition, and crime
markedly improved. But unregulated developing nations now suffer the
worst burden, with 1 in 3 children severely lead poisoned today.
